divergences.en_says: type species B. excelsus based on partial skeleton lacking skull from Como Bluff, Wyoming
divergences.evidence_en: based on a partial skeleton lacking a skull found in Como Bluff, Wyoming

divergences.en_says: B. parvus in 1902 and B. yahnahpin in 1994
divergences.evidence_en: two more species of Brontosaurus were named: B. parvus in 1902 and B. yahnahpin in 1994

divergences.en_says: 2015 study by Emmanuel Tschopp and colleagues; some paleontologists still consider it a synonym
divergences.other_says: 2015 study by joint England-Portugal group; not all paleontologists agree

divergences.en_says: 156 to 146 million years ago during the Kimmeridgian and Tithonian ages
divergences.other_says: Late Jurassic... extinct by end of Jurassic
divergences.evidence_en: lived about 156 to 146 million years ago (mya) during the Kimmeridgian and Tithonian ages

divergences.en_says: robust cervical vertebrae, forelimbs short and stout, hindlimbs elongated; B. excelsus 21–23 m and 15–20 t, B. parvus 19 m
divergences.other_says: long thin neck... up to 15 tons and 22 metres long

divergences.en_says: coexisted with Diplodocus, Barosaurus, Brachiosaurus, Stegosaurus, Allosaurus and others

summary: EN provides more specifics on discovery location, naming dates, anatomy/sizes, coexisting taxa, and study details than MK or IT. IT and EN both note ongoing taxonomic debate but differ on study team description; MK omits the debate entirely. Time ranges are more precise in EN/IT than MK.
